ratings.reviewer_notes: Review-level context on obesity-associated tissue inflammation contributing to insulin resistance, but the abstract does not identify specific human cytokine evidence.
Reviews how pro- and anti-inflammatory cytokines and adipokines may promote obesity-related insulin resistance; human-specific evidence is not described in the abstract.
Focused review of inflammatory cytokines and impaired insulin signaling in skeletal muscle, but the abstract does not establish that the cited evidence comes from human studies.
Reviews cytokine and inflammatory-cell interactions in insulin resistance and mentions human adipose tissue and islets, although the functional evidence highlighted is primarily from mouse knockouts.
Provides indirect human evidence relating vitamin D, cytokine balance, inflammatory markers, and insulin resistance; supplementation findings are described as inconsistent.
PCOS-focused review reporting elevated IL-6 and TNF-alpha and interactions between pro-inflammatory cytokines and insulin resistance, but it is review-level disease-specific evidence.

Human PCOS review discussing inflammatory cytokines and metabolic abnormalities, though the abstract emphasizes PCOS pathogenesis and ovarian dysfunction rather than a specific cytokine–insulin resistance analysis.
The causal TLR4, inflammatory signaling, and insulin-resistance experiments were conducted in cells and mice, not humans.
Broad review linking inflammation and obesity-associated insulin resistance, including anti-inflammatory treatment context, but the abstract provides little cytokine-specific human evidence.
General metabolic syndrome overview that only characterizes the syndrome as proinflammatory with increased cytokine activity; it does not evaluate the cytokine–insulin resistance relationship.
Tirzepatide effects on cytokines, macrophages, and insulin sensitivity were tested in high-fat-fed obese mice rather than humans.
Reviews animal and limited human data suggesting acetate may reduce systemic pro-inflammatory cytokines and affect insulin sensitivity; the abstract explicitly notes that human data are scarce.
Direct human observational evidence: circulating IL-6 correlated with fasting insulin and FIRI, and in a subset was strongly inversely associated with IV glucose-tolerance-test insulin sensitivity.
Direct human study showing greater adipose TNF secretion and plasma IL-6 in obesity, with both inversely related to measured insulin sensitivity, including BMI-matched comparisons.
Cancer-focused review listing inflammatory cytokines and insulin resistance among multiple obesity-related factors without directly evaluating their relationship in humans.

Randomized human crossover trial measuring insulin sensitivity and inflammatory outcomes; overweight participants exposed to carrageenan had lower insulin sensitivity and elevated IL-6 and CRP, with increased cytokine release from participant immune cells.

Mixed human and animal study: the human component related bilirubin mainly to visceral fat, while suppression of TNF-alpha expression and improvement of insulin resistance were demonstrated in obese mice.

Direct experimental human evidence: endotoxin-induced inflammation reduced insulin sensitivity by 35% and induced adipose IL-6, TNF, chemokines, and cytokine-signaling suppressors alongside impaired insulin signaling.

Human adipose-biopsy study linking inflammatory T-cell profiles and cytokine expression to measured systemic insulin resistance; adipose IL-10 expression was inversely associated with insulin resistance.
Review summarizes population associations and proposed TNF-alpha, IL-1, and IL-6 mechanisms connecting inflammation with insulin insensitivity, but is not itself a primary human study.

Large human community study directly measured multiple circulating cytokines and other inflammatory biomarkers against HOMA-IR; the strongest independent associations were for VCAM-1, E-selectin, and CRP rather than cytokines.
Direct human biopsy study showing that adipose inflammation and circulating TNF-alpha and CRP were negatively associated with measured insulin sensitivity in nondiabetic adults.
